title: Two Tens and a Trophy: Williams Wins Lisbon by Twelve
title_candidates: Two Tens and a Trophy: Williams Wins Lisbon by Twelve
The Wipeout Index: Stableford Forgives, Gross Does Not
Blow-Ups by the Atlantic: Williams Takes a Third Trophy, Mullin a Sixth Jacket
Six Men, Nine Double-Figure Holes, One Comfortable Winner
theme: TEG 8 was the tournament of the wipeout hole — sextuple bogeys and double-figure scores scattered across three Lisbon Coast courses — and the two men who won did so on opposite terms with it: Gregg Williams made two 10s and still won the Trophy by 12, because Stableford charges you for one hole and then moves on; David Mullin refused to make one at all and won the Jacket, because gross charges you for every shot.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register; ribbing but never zany, every joke anchored to a scorecard
opening_hook: Open on the ledger of carnage — Williams's 10 at Penha Longa's 12th and his 10 at Quinta da Marinha's 11th — then the reveal that the man who made them won the Trophy by twelve, because Stableford only bills you for the hole; the body is organised around that idea rather than the calendar.
foreshadow: Williams has finished 5th of 5 in the Jacket in each of the last three TEGs — a man who cannot beat anyone at golf but keeps beating everyone at points.
Alex Baker arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, last in both competitions at TEG 7.
Henry Meller arrives as defending Trophy champion (TEG 7), with three prior Spoons already on the shelf.
Stuart Neumann has finished 3rd on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs — the most reliably mid man in TEG history, and never once last.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams — 149 pts, by 12 from Alex Baker
competitions.how: Williams took the outright lead at R1 H10 at Quinta da Marinha and was never headed across the remaining 62 holes — the only lead change of the tournament. He built it rather than inherited it: 38, 41 and 41 were all best in field, he beat Baker head-to-head in three of the four rounds, and the lead went 4, 11, 5, 12. The single wobble was R3 (29 pts, 4th of 6, three behind Baker) — 14 shots bled from the 8th to the 11th including a 10 at the 11th — and the field still only clawed back six of it. R4 at Oitavos settled it early: ten straight holes from the 9th without dropping a net shot and another 41. Even had Alex Baker replaced his worst round with a merely ordinary one, he loses.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin — +77, by 6 from Jon Baker
competitions.how: Mullin led outright from R1 H13 and held it for 36 holes, including a +14 at Penha Longa that was the low gross round of the tournament and six clear at halfway. Then R3 at Quinta da Marinha: his worst TEG round to date on points (26), an 8 at the 12th, and at the 13th Jon Baker took the lead away from him. Baker still led by two standing on the 18th tee — and lost it there. At Oitavos, Mullin retook the lead outright at the 2nd and buried it: +17, eight strokes better than Baker, an 8 at the 11th absorbed and a birdie at the 16th to stop the bleeding. Three best-in-field rounds, never worse than 3rd, steadier than anyone: built, not gifted.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Stuart Neumann — 100 pts, last by 11 from Henry Meller
competitions.how: Neumann went to the bottom at R1 H4 and stayed there for all 72 holes — bottom of the field in every single round, the only man in the six never to post a round above the median. R1 set the tone: 17 points, +43 gross, 29 shots bled between the 7th and the 15th. R3 finished it: 17 shots gone in the opening five holes, a 10 at the 1st, a 9 at the 4th, an 8 at the 9th and an 11 at the 10th, for 20 points and a 14-point hiding from Meller. The cruelty is that it was partly inherited — Meller outplayed him over two of the four rounds and finished 11 adrift anyway, because Meller's R4 at Oitavos was worse than anything even Neumann managed.

headline_candidates: Oitavos Dunes: Mullin Takes the Jacket Back at the Second and Never Gives It Up

Ten Clean Holes to the House: Williams Signs for 41 and a Third Trophy
rounds.chosen_headline: Oitavos Dunes: Mullin Takes the Jacket Back at the Second, Williams Cruises Home
rounds.angle: A links finish that rewarded exactly one kind of golf: Mullin retakes the gross lead at the 2nd and wins the round by eight, Williams plays the last ten without dropping a net shot for 41 and a twelve-point win, and the defending Trophy champion drops 22 shots in six holes.

players.arc: Two prior Trophies and three consecutive last-place Jacket finishes, and here is the purest expression of the type: two 10s, one dreadful R3, three best-in-field rounds and a third Trophy by twelve.
Back-to-back Jacket holder makes it three and six overall — the only man in the field who never once made a double-figure score, which is precisely why he won the competition that counts them all.
Arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, leaves as Trophy runner-up, having made a 10 at the hardest hole on the course in R3 and a 9 at the last in R4 — improvement in TEG is rarely tidy.
Led the Jacket by two with one hole of R3 to play, gave it back on the 18th green, then lost R4 to Mullin by eight — beaten in three of four rounds and second again, which is becoming his genre.

Defending Trophy champion whose title defence expired somewhere between the 2nd and the 5th at Oitavos, where 22 shots vanished in six holes, including a 10 and a 9 — and he still avoided the Spoon by eleven.
Third on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs, and now bottom of the field in every round of this one: 17, 31, 20, 32, a Spoon by eleven, and an R4 32 that arrived four days too late.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to the Lisbon Coast, and a neat family outing: R1 and R3 on Robert Trent Jones Sr.'s parkland at Quinta da Marinha (new to TEG in R1, played twice), R2 on his son's mountain layout at Penha Longa in the Sintra hills, R4 on Arthur Hills's Atlantic links at Oitavos Dunes. Use the father-and-son framing once, lightly; use Penha Longa's steepness to set up Mullin's 86 as the low gross round of the tournament; save the pure-links exposure of Oitavos for R4, where it flattered Mullin and Williams and dismembered Meller.
course_history_notes: Every course was new to TEG this trip, so all six were playing blind — Quinta da Marinha was the only one seen twice, in R1 and again in R3.
Quinta da Marinha's best return of the tournament was Jon Baker's 89 in R3; its worst was Neumann's 114 in R1.
Penha Longa, billed as the hardest of the three, produced the lowest gross round anyone shot all tournament: Mullin's 86 in R2.
Oitavos Dunes yielded a 25-shot spread on the closing day, from Mullin's 88 to Meller's 111.
decisive_moments: Trophy — R2 at Penha Longa: Williams's 41 pushed the lead from 4 to 11; he had taken it outright at R1 H10 and nobody got within five of him again.
Green Jacket — R4 H2 at Oitavos Dunes: Mullin retook the gross lead outright from Jon Baker and never lost it, winning the round by eight.
Wooden Spoon — R3 at Quinta da Marinha: Neumann's 17 shots dropped in the opening five holes, and a 20-point round that left him 14 behind Meller with only Oitavos remaining.
(Ordering note for the writer: Trophy, Jacket, Spoon, in that order.)

payoffs.payoff: He makes 10s at R2 H12 and R3 H11, finishes nowhere near Mullin's +77 on gross — and wins the Trophy by twelve, because a Stableford card charges you for one hole and then hands you a fresh one.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker as reigning Wooden Spoon holder
payoffs.payoff: Runner-up on 137, seven clean holes at Oitavos from the 8th to the 14th, and the Spoon passed to a man who had never held it — despite Baker's own 10 at the SI 1 8th in R3.

payoffs.seed: Meller the defending Trophy champion with three prior Spoons
payoffs.payoff: 22 shots gone in the first six holes at Oitavos — a 10 at the 4th, a 9 at the SI 1 5th, four blank holes in a row — for 21 points, 13 down on his R3; the defence ends with him closer to the Spoon than the Trophy.

payoffs.seed: Neumann 3rd on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs, never last
payoffs.payoff: Bottom of the field in all four rounds and the Spoon by eleven — the run of thirds ends in the least dignified direction available.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as the prominent frame: nine double-figure holes across six players is the actual texture of TEG 8, and cataloguing them is what makes the Williams/Mullin contrast land — the man with the most wipeouts won the points, the man with none won the gross.

why_the_champion_won: Built, not inherited: three best-in-field rounds (38, 41, 41) either side of one below-median 29, head-to-head wins over Alex Baker in three of the four rounds, and a scoring format that billed him only two zeros for his two 10s — even Baker playing to his own average doesn't flip it.
